assumptions: A suitably scoped Polish legal opinion can support a no-custody advisory and orchestration role without the venture itself becoming a collector, processor, transporter, seller, or product-safety responsible party.
Some planned commercial string-inverter removals retain enough avoidable handling cost, compliance risk, or resale value for a pre-removal route decision to matter to the installer.
The family installer can provide bounded pilot access, but this is not assumed to imply paid adoption, repeat use, exclusivity, or a transferable sales channel.
Professional buyers and authorized operators could return decision-grade quotes within installation planning windows, although no response-time commitment is evidenced.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A Polish counsel opinion on the exact no-custody flow, signed buyer and authorized-operator service-level terms, and a consecutive paid pilot showing conversion, repeat use, removal density, route outcomes, response times, disputes or returns, and fully loaded contribution margin independently of salvage proceeds.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Placing the decision before removal is a coherent response to the legal boundary between used equipment and WEEE: title, condition, and route evidence can preserve lawful options before physical handling narrows them. The packet does not establish that this information gap is currently unmanaged or valuable enough to support a separate business.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Misclassification, disposal coordination, and lost residual value can plausibly create installer pain, especially on scheduled replacement jobs. However, no installer has accepted a fee, and existing operators may already provide adequate routing as part of their downstream service, leaving the severity and separable willingness to pay uncertain.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: No custody, no inventory, and a fixed fee that must stand without salvage are disciplined economic choices with limited capital exposure. Yet price, job frequency, labor per exception, partner cost, conversion, repeat rate, gross margin, CAC, payback, and liability allocation are all unknown, while the cited downstream activity is characterized as high-volume and low-return.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: One inverter class in a dense service area is narrow enough for a controlled pilot and avoids premature breadth. Its economic significance is unproven because neither removal density nor the reusable share, fee pool, or number of suitable installer accounts is established.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Embedding at the pre-removal work-order checkpoint is a potentially useful position, but the venture has no mandate, exclusive supply, proprietary rights, or contracted channel. PV CYCLE and SecondSol already cover major portions of compliance, collection, testing, repair, logistics, recycling, and resale, and could plausibly add or absorb this checkpoint.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A proven routing record could extend to other installer clusters, regions, or renewable-energy equipment classes. Each expansion would introduce different condition tests, buyer liquidity, safety duties, waste rules, and partner networks, so the initial workflow does not automatically unlock low-friction adjacency.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Serial-level outcomes could eventually improve routing and partner selection, but no proprietary dataset exists and ordinary workflow data alone is unlikely to prevent replication. Installers, authorized operators, marketplaces, or software vendors can copy the evidence pack unless contracts, embedded integrations, or privileged supply access emerge.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: The proposed gate may offer convenience, an auditable record, and a conservative fallback route without taking inventory risk. The packet provides no measured reduction in installer time, liability, disposal cost, or increase in recovery value relative to direct use of existing operators, so behavior-changing superiority remains uncertain.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Rising PV-system waste and reuse activity, combined with documentation and product-safety duties, makes disposition increasingly relevant. Immature second-hand assessment guidance also slows transactions and increases liability, so the same timing force creates both demand potential and adoption friction.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: The family installer offers unusually low-friction access to a bounded first workflow and enables direct measurement without broad marketing. There is no paid commitment, exclusivity, or evidence that other installers can be acquired repeatably and affordably, and founder-led B2B coordination may become socially and operationally intensive.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The standardized, no-custody pilot is compatible with the founder's data and automation skills, available capital, and part-time constraints. Material legal-advisory exposure, partner response dependency, title and product-status exceptions, warranty allocation, sparse jobs, and dispute handling remain, and several cannot be automated away.

highest_value_structural_change: Convert the optional one-off checkpoint into a contracted, white-label route-decision layer embedded across an installer cluster's replacement workflow, backed by an authorized operator and professional buyer with quote-time service levels, minimum job volume, and clear liability allocation; this would address distribution, density, repeat revenue, and data access together.
main_structural_strength: The pre-removal, no-custody gate puts evidence and route selection at the moment when lawful options can still be preserved, while keeping regulated physical activity and inventory risk with authorized counterparties.
primary_score_limiter: There is no evidence that installers will pay enough, often enough, for a separate checkpoint to cover fully loaded coordination and liability costs, and the proposed distribution point is neither contracted nor exclusive.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: PV CYCLE and SecondSol already span much of the compliance, collection, testing, repair, logistics, resale, and recycling stack, directly weakening the claim that a separate routing layer has a durable control point or unmet paid demand.
